# Root review correction before board invocation

Do not require uptime/counter continuity with E73's previous closed UART session. Opening the existing BoardSession may toggle reset lines even with DTR/RTS handling. A reboot during opening is authorized and does not erase the retained LittleFS contents; it starts a new measurement epoch. The two passes within THIS owned session must be continuous.

Current capture_repeat.py calls no_boot(initial) and initializes previous from the old E73 final snapshot; that can reject a healthy board before work. Instead retain initial boot output, report whether opening booted/reset the time/counters (or continuity cannot be proven), use the first stable stat snapshot of this owned session as its epoch baseline, and compare subsequent snapshots only to that. You may compare to old E73 data for classification, not as a mandatory cumulative-delta gate. Document that a new boot changes mount/allocation starting conditions and prevents a cross-session continuity claim. Never ignore reboot, lost counters, or generation reset DURING the two-pass experiment. Preserve failure raw data and fail before destructive work if first snapshot is invalid. Prefer baseline/stat before mkdir so this gate precedes writes.

Keep this a minimal correction, with one meaningful initial-boot/new-epoch case and one mid-run reboot/counter-reset rejection. No board use by worker; all other task scope unchanged.

I’ll make the first valid stat in this owned session establish the measurement epoch before mkdir. Opening boot output will be retained and classified; resets or counter loss after that baseline will still abort the experiment. I’ll update the two epoch checks and hashes without using the board.

The correction passes all eight offline checks. The opening-boot case completes both passes with a new baseline below the old session’s counters; an invalid first stat stops before mkdir. Mid-run boot, counter loss, generation reset and migration still abort with raw data preserved. I’m refreshing the ready manifest now.
